question: What three disciplines are integrated within nursing informatics?

options.A: Medicine, hardware engineering, and data analytics
options.C: Public health, statistics, and software development
options.D: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: Nursing informatics is explicitly defined by the combination of nursing science, computer science, and information science to manage health data. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is nursing informatics considered more than just using computers in a hospital?

options.A: It requires advanced programming skills to build custom hospital software
options.B: It focuses on how technology shapes clinical workflows and patient outcomes
options.C: It is exclusively managed by hospital IT departments without clinical input
options.D: It eliminates the need for any direct patient bedside interaction

explanation: Informatics goes beyond basic computer literacy by examining how digital systems interact with clinical judgment, workflows, and care quality. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which technology scans patient wristbands and medication packages to verify medication administration?
explanation: Bar Code Medication Administration directly verifies the right patient, drug, dose, route, and time right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h2)

question: A nurse receives an automated pop-up warning on the computer screen indicating that a prescribed drug interacts severely with the patient's documented allergy. What system generated this alert?
explanation: Clinical Decision Support Systems analyze patient data against rules and guidelines to provide real-time safety alerts like allergy warnings. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of electronic documentation over traditional paper records?

options.A: Instant availability of data to authorized team members
options.B: Automatic diagnosis of complex medical conditions
options.C: No requirement for staff training or password security
options.D: Complete elimination of clinical documentation errors

explanation: Digital charts allow multiple users across different units to view and update patient records simultaneously without physical transport delays. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h3)

question: How do structured templates and drop-down menus improve daily workflow efficiency for nurses?

options.A: By preventing patients from accessing their own medical histories
options.B: By standardizing data entry and reducing repetitive manual writing
options.C: By replacing all critical thinking with automated nursing care
options.D: By removing the need to record vital signs during night shifts

explanation: Structured data entry speeds up the charting process while keeping terminology consistent across the unit. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h3)

question: What term describes the centralized digital record where all healthcare disciplines update patient findings simultaneously?
explanation: A centralized electronic record acts as a single source of truth, ensuring everyone views the most current patient information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is real-time cross-disciplinary communication vital in clinical settings?

options.A: It accelerates response times to critical results and prevents care fragmentation
options.B: It eliminates the need for face-to-face shift change handovers entirely
options.C: It allows nurses to override physician orders without consultation
options.D: It ensures that patients never have to speak directly with doctors

explanation: Instant sharing of diagnostics and notes helps different teams coordinate interventions quickly and safely. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does informatics directly support evidence-based practice at the bedside?

options.A: By providing instant digital access to clinical guidelines and research databases
options.B: By restricting clinical data access to senior hospital administrators
options.C: By mandating paper-based literature searches for every shift
options.D: By replacing clinical judgment with rigid robotic algorithms

explanation: Workstation integration lets clinicians consult current evidence and protocols immediately while planning patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the benefit of aggregating large volumes of patient data within electronic health systems?

options.A: It guarantees that medical errors will never occur again
options.B: It enables researchers to identify successful care trends and improve institutional protocols
options.C: It reduces the total number of nursing staff required on duty
options.D: It allows the hospital to sell patient information to commercial advertisers

explanation: Large datasets reveal patterns that help healthcare facilities refine care bundles and elevate overall quality standards. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h5)

question: What mechanism restricts staff members to viewing only the patient records necessary for their specific job functions?
explanation: Role-based access controls limit system privileges based on a user's professional role, protecting patient confidentiality. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: What purpose do digital audit logs serve in electronic health record systems?

options.A: They delete old patient records after twenty-four hours
options.B: They automatically calculate staff monthly salaries and overtime hours
options.C: They measure the physical walking speed of nurses during their shifts
options.D: They track who accessed a patient file and what changes were made, ensuring accountability

explanation: Audit logs record every interaction with a patient record, helping security teams monitor for unauthorized access. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is direct nursing input crucial when designing and implementing new health technologies?

options.A: Technology adoption is legally impossible without a nursing signature
options.B: Nurses understand both technical system capabilities and real patient care needs
options.C: Nurses are the only professionals permitted to purchase hospital software
options.D: Software engineers cannot write code without nursing supervision

explanation: Clinical experience ensures that digital tools fit smoothly into actual bedside workflows instead of creating obstacles. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a modern digital health trend mentioned in contemporary nursing practice?

options.B: Manual carbon-paper duplication of all medical charts

explanation: Manual carbon-paper duplication represents outdated paper-based systems, whereas modern digital trends focus on automation, AI, and connectivity. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h7)
